_comment: Independent-implementability ledger (SPEC §13). One record per blind
implementation attempt. This file is an ASSERTION about runs that happened;
scripts/check-implementability.py machine-checks the half that can be checked
— that each surface_digest is exactly what blind-export.py reproduces from the
recorded source — and enforces the structural rules §13 states. The verdict
itself is attested by the implementer and cannot be re-derived by CI, which is
why it carries the evidence pointer rather than standing alone.
Rounds are append-only. A superseded verdict is never edited: it is a fact
about a surface that existed, and later repair does not make it untrue.

rounds.surface_note: NOT RECORDED. This run predates blind-export.py and ran in a git worktree, so the supplied surface was not pinned by a manifest and cannot be reconstructed exactly. Per §13.3 the claim is therefore unbound, and is retained as history rather than as evidence.

rounds.implementer_statement: A working implementation exists and reproduces 23 of 25 vectors on its first run. But several encoding details were not determined by the prose, and two fixtures are not reproducible from the specification at all.
rounds.constructive_note: On failing to reproduce two published fixtures the implementer searched over 160,000 candidate encodings, declined to infer the missing sentinel, and reported the fixtures as irreproducible rather than adjusting until they matched. 23/25 carrying that refusal is stronger evidence than 25/25 obtained by adaptation: it is the first round demonstrating resistance to teaching-to-the-test, and it is what exposed an undocumented constant in the reference.

rounds.hypothesis: The declared normative surface — this document plus the normative data §13.1b incorporates — is now sufficient for an independent implementation of §12 WITHOUT INFERENCE. Recorded BEFORE dispatch so it is falsifiable rather than narrated afterwards: if the round returns PASS-WITH-INFERENCE, this hypothesis is disproved and the inferred list says exactly where the surface is still incomplete.
rounds.prediction: If a defect is found it will most likely NOT be in licensing. §13.1a/§13.1b created a new abstraction — the prose/normative-data boundary — and this run is its first independent user, so the likeliest findings are that a declared schema constrains one thing and not another, that an artifact's interpretation is still implied rather than stated, or that the versioning rule is underspecified.
rounds.constructive_note: Three vectors turn on one undetermined clause — what to EMIT for an unrecognised policy. The implementer identified that both readings satisfy the stated rule, declined to adopt the fixtures' reading because doing so would be inference, and left the vectors failing. It also ran the alternative reading in a separate probe, confirmed all three reproduce exactly under it, and did not modify the implementation.
rounds.prediction_outcome: PARTLY CONFIRMED. The prediction was that findings would fall at the prose/normative-data boundary. The implementer called that boundary 'the best-specified part of §12' — so the prediction was wrong about where the WEAKNESS was — but it still yielded three real defects there: model retrieval unspecified, consumer behaviour on a malformed model undefined, and no obligation to RECOMPUTE model-digest. The largest findings were elsewhere: the identity never bound its subject.

rounds.implementer_statement: A working implementation came out of the prose plus model.json, but eleven things were not determined by them, and I left three vectors failing rather than tune to them.

rounds.research_question: Does the implementability methodology GENERALISE across independently evolved sections? Four rounds matured §12 and each found a new defect class, but the methodology was validated only on the section receiving all the attention. §8.6 is the harder test: 8/18 obligations witnessed, one prior blind implementation, much older design decisions, and dense interaction with identity, signatures, journals and conformance. If the method depends on licensing it should visibly fail here.
rounds.hypothesis: §8.6, on this surface, is NOT yet independently implementable without inference — predicted from its lower witnessed coverage, not from any audit. The stronger claim under test is not about §8.6 at all: it is that the METHOD produces the same quality of finding on a section it was not developed against.

taxonomy_hypothesis.claim: Every finding will fall into one of the four defect classes §12 produced. A FIFTH class would be the more valuable outcome: it would show the taxonomy is §12-shaped rather than general.
classes: 1. MISSING MEANING — the document does not say enough to proceed honestly
2. HIDDEN NORMATIVE INPUTS — meaning exists but lives in fixtures or implementation, not the declared surface
3. INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY — enough is communicated to implement, but the document contradicts itself or leans on undocumented constants
4. INCOMPLETELY DEFINED OBJECTS — every field is correct and the encoding still does not say what it identifies
taxonomy_hypothesis.method: The taxonomy is deliberately WITHHELD from the dispatch brief. Supplying it would shape what the subject looks for and convert a test of the taxonomy into a confirmation of it. Findings are classified afterwards, by us, against the list recorded here.

rounds.prediction: Specific pre-registered guess, recorded so it can lose: §8.6.4a requires rejecting a small-order public key and neither lists the encodings nor states how to derive them, so a blind implementation cannot obtain them from the surface. That would be class 2 (hidden normative inputs) — the same class round two found in §12, appearing independently in a section developed years apart. Noted BEFORE dispatch and deliberately NOT repaired first, since pre-repairing is teaching to the test.

interpretation.why: Deciding how to READ each possible outcome after seeing one is the same defect as writing a hypothesis after the result. Recorded here so no outcome can be reframed into a success, and so a clean result cannot be quietly discounted as a null one.
interpretation.what_generalisation_requires: NOT that the same defects recur. That is the weaker claim, and the recurrence prediction below tests only it. Generalisation requires the PROCESS to expose specification insufficiency on a section it was not developed against, without relying on licensing-specific machinery and without prior hints.

readings.class 2 reproduces (small-order or other: a defect class found in §12 recurring in an independently evolved domain — evidence the taxonomy is general rather than §12-shaped
readings.all findings map onto the four classes: the taxonomy holds on a section it was not derived from; stronger than any individual recurrence
readings.a FIFTH class appears: the most valuable outcome. The taxonomy was §12-shaped and is now larger. Record the new class and re-examine §12 for instances of it
readings.genuinely inference-free PASS: POSITIVE, not null. It would show the method can DISTINGUISH a mature section from an immature one rather than mechanically generating findings — which is the failure mode a process like this is most at risk of. Only counts if the derivation log holds up: expert knowledge filling a silent spec is inference, and a correct implementation built from undocumented prior knowledge is still evidence the specification was insufficient
readings.the methodology itself breaks on \u00a78: a real result, not a failed run. It would mean the method depends on properties §12 happened to have — most likely a fixture family that cannot express what the section does, which §12 already hit once at LICENSE-CLOSURE-EXCLUSIVE
